frame.part: top of the page, no scrolling

summary: The new Met Office place page: the next hour in very large type, three chips, ten day tabs, an hourly table that gives the gust its own row. No UK warning was in force, so the warning banner was not seen.

callouts.title: Five views of one forecast
callouts.does_well: Daily, Detailed, Map, Long range, UK: the same place at five depths, as tabs.
callouts.fed_by: our two faces: the weather face and the data room

callouts.title: The next hour, very large
callouts.does_well: "NEXT HOUR 9°C Light rain": the page answers "what now" before anything else.

callouts.title: Three chips, one of them the gust
callouts.does_well: "Feels like 7°", "Light rain ≥95%", "Max gust 19mph from the northeast": the gust is named in the summary, in words, with its direction.

callouts.title: Ten day tabs; the far ones marked BETA
callouts.does_well: High and low per day; days eight to ten carry a "BETA" label: lower confidence is marked on the tab itself.

callouts.title: The hourly table, gust on its own row
callouts.does_well: Per hour: symbol, temperature, feels like, chance of rain, mean wind with arrow, and under it the gust. Mean wind and gust are never confused.

callouts.title: When it was updated
callouts.does_well: "Updated: 1am on 11 November 2026", directly under the table.
callouts.fed_by: read_utc and next_read_utc of every file
